exposure: Disclosure of SV history to a maternity care provider
cohort: The study included 10,867 women who had given birth in the 5 years prior to completing a nationwide questionnaire.
finding: Disclosure of sexual violence history to a maternity care provider is associated with specific birth interventions, such as a reduced likelihood of episiotomy and an increased likelihood of unplanned cesarean birth, but does not improve the overall birth experience for women.
mod_finding: Respondents who disclosed their SV history had lower adjusted odds of episiotomy, while primiparous respondents with disclosed SV history had increased odds of unplanned cesarean birth compared to spontaneous and assisted vaginal birth.
cross-section timing: Data was collected from women who had given birth in the 5 years prior to completing the questionnaire.
